hero.headline: We put artificial intelligence to work inside your operation.
hero.sub: Osppy is an applied-AI company from Guadalajara. Applied means this: a concrete task, a written process, a system that does it on its own, and a result you review.
hero.ctaMessage: Hi, I'd like to talk about my business operations.

diagrama.pie: The step almost nobody has written down is the second one.
diagrama.alt: Four-step diagram: the task goes through a process written by someone, an agent carries it out, and it produces a result.

somos.headline: Systems running in real businesses today.
somos.p1: Osppy is an applied artificial-intelligence company from Guadalajara. We work with businesses of every size that want to use AI with judgment: to remove repetitive work, bring order to the operation, and stop everything from depending on the owner.
somos.p2: Osppy's systems run in real businesses today. What we recommend doesn't come from a conference stage: it comes from building, delivering, and keeping systems running.
somos.p3: There are three ways into an operation: train the team, advise on where AI is worth it — and where it isn't — and implement systems that stay running.
somos.cita: Artificial intelligence proposes. A person reviews and decides.
somos.citaNota: The principle behind everything we build.

capacitacion.body: Hands-on workshops for owners and teams: you leave able to apply something today, working on real tasks from your business. First we teach people to use the tools well; then we watch which problems keep coming back.
capacitacion.f3Value: The intro talk and the first workshop are written; the first groups are about to open
capacitacion.f4Value: Quoted per group and per outcome

asesoria.body: Sessions on how to make AI useful in your business. The first one is almost always a diagnostic: understanding your operation and finding where we can help. Sometimes the answer is training; sometimes it's putting a process in order; sometimes it's building.
asesoria.preguntasTitulo: The diagnostic starts with questions like:
preguntas: Where does your team's time actually go?
Which process repeats the same way every week?
What information do you already have that nobody is using?
What's worth automating — and what isn't yet?

implementacion.body: We build systems that stay running inside your operation — from a quoting tool to an agent that does the whole task on its own — with scope and success criteria in writing. After delivery, there are hosting, monitoring, and maintenance plans.
tipos: Models in your own infrastructure, with Amazon Bedrock

como.headline: Understand first. Building comes last.
como.p1Body: We get to know your operation and find where AI genuinely helps — and where it isn't needed.
como.p2Body: Before anything gets built, the process gets written down. It's the step almost nobody has done, and everything else depends on it.
como.p3Body: Quoted separately, with scope and success criteria in writing. No promises of savings, sales, or hours: the impact is measured by your numbers.
como.p4Body: What we deliver can stay under a hosting, monitoring, and maintenance plan, depending on what your operation needs.

trayectoria.headline: What has been done.
trayectoria.agentes: Also: agents that do the whole task on their own — autonomous — running in production systems today.
trayectoria.nota: “+100” and “+50” are the operator's own estimate as of 2026-09-02; no formal records exist for that stage.

casos.headline: The work can be told without names.
casos.body: No client is named here without written permission, and no figure is published without measurement. What we can say: the kind of work that has been delivered.
casos.t1Body: Systems that put a quote together using the business's own rules and prices, so it doesn't depend on one person.
casos.t2Body: They do a whole task on their own — autonomous — inside a defined process, with written rules.
casos.t3Body: They answer and attend with the information the business loads. If something isn't there, they say so or ask — they don't make things up.
casos.t4Body: Getting a whole team working with an enterprise-grade AI tool, with order and rules of use.
casos.t5Body: When the information can't leave your house, the model is deployed inside your own infrastructure, with Amazon Bedrock.
casos.t6Body: The groundwork: getting the process written down before automating anything. Without it, we don't build agents.
casos.t7Body: A diagnostic of the operation and a map of where AI helps — and where it doesn't.
casos.giros: Delivered across industries like construction, logistics, furniture stores, retail, private schools, and online businesses.

productos.headline: Two products, each with its own page.

testimonios.headline: Illustrative voices from people who use an assistant like this.
testimonios.nota: Quotes without names and without figures: they illustrate what it's like to have an assistant answering. They are not verified testimonials.
testimonios.q1: I used to answer messages at midnight every single day. Now I sleep. The assistant replies in my tone, with my business's exact information.
testimonios.q2: I thought a bot would feel fake. Not at all: my clients write to it the same way they write to me, and it knows when to hand the conversation over.
testimonios.q3: I stopped losing bookings to slow replies. What comes in overnight no longer goes unanswered.

faq.headline: What we usually get asked.
faq.a1: That artificial intelligence doesn't stay in a demo. It goes to work inside the operation: a concrete task, from a concrete role, with a result someone reviews.
faq.a2: Almost always with a diagnostic: understanding your operation and finding where AI genuinely helps. What follows depends on what shows up: training, putting a process in order, or building a system.
faq.q3: What if my processes aren't written down anywhere?
faq.a3: That's the most common case. Structuring the process is part of the work — and it comes before any automation. We don't build agents without well-defined processes.
faq.a4: We don't promise savings, sales, or hours: your numbers measure that. We don't hand over a tool and walk away. And our systems don't confirm prices, availability, or terms nobody verified: when they don't know something, they say so, they ask, or they hand the conversation to a person.
faq.a5: We define in writing what information can be used, what gets anonymized, and what stays out. And AI tools do get things wrong sometimes: that's why everything is set up so a person can review and decide.
faq.a6: Training and advisory are quoted per group and per outcome; implementation separately, with scope and success criteria in writing. We don't publish prices because we don't sell packages: every proposal is about your case.

cta.headline: Tell us about your operation.
cta.body: You write to us, a person answers, and we see if there's something worth doing. Sometimes the honest answer is “not yet” — we'll give you that one too.
